name: IC-706MKII
subtitle: Operating reference
kicker: Independent operating reference. Not an Icom publication and not affiliated with Icom.
verified: Written from the radio and its manual by K4DIA. Menu behavior differs on the MKIIG.
keys: Split. Long press to enable; transmit moves to VFO B.
Swap VFO A and VFO B.
Memory write. Hold two seconds to store the current VFO.
VFO and memory toggle. M-CH dial selects the channel.
Copy the selected memory into the VFO. Memory clear in memory mode.
Filter select. Cycles the filters actually installed.
Noise blanker. Built for ignition noise, not for hash.
AGC fast and slow. SSB and AM only.
Receive incremental tuning. Clear it before you forget it is on.
Scan start and stop. Set the squelch first.
Band stack. Hold a band key to recall its stored frequencies.
Set mode. Long press DISPLAY to enter from any mode.
quick: Set it per band and per site. Write it in the Site Record.
Mic gain, CW pitch, RTTY tone
The encode tone the repeater wants.
Only opens on a matching tone. Different from Q6.
filters: The default. Everything you work on phone.
Worth fitting. Turns a crowded 40 m evening into a workable one.
Worth fitting if you work CW at all. It is the difference between hearing one signal and three.
Wide. Shortwave listening, not much else.
specs: 160 through 6 m, plus 2 m. No 70 cm on the MKII.
13.8 V DC, 20 A at full HF output
CI-V on the REMOTE jack, 3.5 mm
tasks: VFO mode. Set frequency, mode, offset and tone. Pick a channel with the M-CH dial. Hold MW for two seconds.
Set the output frequency, the shift, and the encode tone in Q6. Listen before you call. On a linked system wait a beat after keying.
Set your transmit frequency in VFO B, long press SPL. Check where you are actually transmitting before you call.
Partial reset keeps memories. Full reset does not. Do the partial one first, and only reach for the full reset when you have written your memories down.
Set mode. UTC, always. Every field in this book assumes it.
trouble: No transmit on a band you should have
Check the band edge first, then the mode, then whether the tuner is faulted. The radio will refuse quietly.
Encode tone in Q6, not tone squelch in Q7. They are different settings and Q7 will make you deaf as well as silent.
Computer will not see the radio
CI-V address, then baud, then transceive, then the cable. In that order, one at a time.
Receive is deaf on one band
Check the preamp and the attenuator before you suspect the antenna.
Partial reset. Write your memories down first, every time.
notes: Run it at the power the contact needs, not the power the radio has. Every watt above what works is amp-hours you do not get back.
The finals get hot on a long CW or digital run with no airflow. Give it a fan or give it a rest.
It draws about 20 A key down at 100 W. Fuse and wire for that even if you never use it.
The internal tuner is an option, not a fitting. Know which one you have before you plan an antenna around it.
Detachable head means the connector is a failure point. Carry the spare separation cable or accept that a bad day ends early.
control: REMOTE, 3.5 mm on the rear panel
Read it from set mode on the radio. The 706 family uses a different address per model, and the MKIIG is 58h.
Set mode. 19200 is the usual choice; drop it if the link is flaky.
Set mode. On means the radio announces changes unasked.
CI-V is not RS-232. Use a CT-17 or an equivalent interface; a bare serial cable will not work.
